title: Case studies: East & North Africa
intro: The four cases below cover East and North Africa. Three meet the success criteria: M-KOPA (asset financing), MNT-Halan (digital lending) and NALA (cross-border payments). The fourth, Sendy, a logistics company that closed in 2023, is the cautionary case. Three regional features shape capital strategy: mobile money dominates East African payments, Egypt has absorbed repeated devaluations since 2016, and DFIs are active in both regions.

rows.name: M-KOPA
rows.sub: Kenya · Fintech: asset financing and digital credit

rows.name: MNT-Halan
rows.sub: Egypt · Fintech with logistics roots: digital lending, payments, e-commerce, delivery

rows.name: Sendy
rows.sub: Kenya · Logistics: on-demand delivery, then B2B transport, fulfilment and supply

title: Case studies: West Africa
intro: The five case studies below examine founders in West African markets, with Nigeria as the primary anchor. Two are scaled companies (Moniepoint and LemFi) and three are early-stage (Autogirl, Feegor and Earthbond). They apply the same analytical framework as the East and North Africa cases, enabling cross-regional comparison in the synthesis that follows.

rows.name: Moniepoint
rows.sub: Nigeria · Business payments and banking; licensed microfinance bank

rows.name: Autogirl (Muvment by Autogirl)
rows.sub: Nigeria and Ghana · Peer-to-peer vehicle rental marketplace

rows.name: Moove
rows.sub: Nigeria · Vehicle financing for ride-hailing drivers

rows.name: LemFi
rows.sub: Nigeria · Cross-border payments for the diaspora
